concept.name: Process orientation
concept.definition: An evaluative stance that judges trading performance by the quality of decisions and adherence to process rather than by individual trade outcomes. It is the deliberate correction for outcome bias, on the principle that in probabilistic domains good processes produce good results only on average, not on any single trial.
concept.intuition: You cannot control whether this trade wins; you can control whether it was a good trade - so grade the decision, not the dollar result.
concept.mechanics: Operationalized by defining controllable process elements (setup selection, entry timing, sizing, exit execution, review), scoring each trade on those elements, and aggregating process metrics separately from P&L. Bellafiore's 'one good trade' framework institutionalizes the stance: a trade is good if it followed the rules, whatever its result.
concept.failure_modes: Taken too far it can immunize a failing strategy from evidence: 'process was fine' must eventually reconcile with long-run expectancy or the process definition is wrong. Process scores are also themselves vulnerable to self-serving grading.
concept.misconceptions: Process orientation does not mean outcomes are irrelevant - aggregate outcomes are the test of the process. It is also not positive thinking; it is measurement discipline applied to decisions under uncertainty.
concept.example: A trader loses on three consecutive well-executed A-setups and changes nothing; the next month the same process recovers, confirming the losses were variance, not error.
